description.en: Say what people look like and what they are like, talk about how you feel, and make adjectives agree with people.
description.so: Sheeg sida dadku u eg yihiin iyo dabeecaddooda, ka hadal sida aad dareemayso, oo sifooyinka la waafaji dadka.

body.en: Swahili adjectives change with the noun. For people they take m- for one person and wa- for more than one: mtu mrefu (a tall person), watu warefu (tall people); mtoto mzuri, watoto wazuri. If the adjective starts with a vowel, m- becomes mw- and wa- joins it: mwembamba, wembamba (thin). This works for every word about a person, even nouns that look different, such as kaka or rafiki: Kaka yangu ni mrefu.
body.so: Sifooyinka Sawaaxiligu way isbeddelaan iyadoo ku xiran magaca. Dadka, waxay qaataan m- hal qof iyo wa- wax ka badan hal qof: mtu mrefu (qof dheer), watu warefu (dad dhaadheer); mtoto mzuri, watoto wazuri. Haddii sifadu ku bilaabato shaqal, m- waxay noqotaa mw-, wa-na way ku biirtaa: mwembamba, wembamba (caato). Tani waxay khusaysaa eray kasta oo qof ku saabsan, xataa magacyo u eg kuwo kale sida kaka ama rafiki: Kaka yangu ni mrefu.

examples.so: Walaalahay hablaha ahi way dhaadheer yihiin.

title.so: Waa, wuxuu leeyahay, iyo u eg

body.en: Use ni for what someone is: Ni mfupi. Use ana (he/she has) for features: Ana ndevu. With body words the adjective agrees with the thing, not the person: Ana nywele ndefu (long hair). Anafanana na means 'looks like', and kuliko means 'than': Ni mrefu kuliko mimi (He's taller than me).
body.so: Isticmaal ni waxa qofku yahay: Ni mfupi. Isticmaal ana (wuxuu leeyahay) astaamaha: Ana ndevu. Erayada jirka, sifadu waxay la socotaa shayga, ma aha qofka: Ana nywele ndefu (timo dhaadheer). Anafanana na waxay ka dhigan tahay 'u eg', kuliko-na waa 'ka': Ni mrefu kuliko mimi (Wuu iga dheer yahay).

body.en: Many feeling verbs use -me-, the 'have become' tense: nimechoka (I'm tired, lit. I have got tired), nimefurahi (I'm happy), nimekasirika (I'm angry). With a feeling noun use nina (I have): nina hasira (I'm angry), nina wasiwasi (I'm worried). Naogopa (I'm scared) is the everyday short form of ninaogopa.
body.so: Falal badan oo dareen ah waxay isticmaalaan -me-, waqtiga 'noqday': nimechoka (waan daallanahay, macnaha: waan daalay), nimefurahi (waan faraxsanahay), nimekasirika (waan cadhooday). Magac dareen ah waxaa lagu isticmaalaa nina (waxaan qabaa): nina hasira (waan cadhaysanahay), nina wasiwasi (waan walwalsanahay). Naogopa (waan baqayaa) waa qaabka gaaban ee maalinlaha ah ee ninaogopa.

body.en: Umependeza! (You look nice!) is the safest compliment, for clothes, a new hairstyle or a special day. Comments on weight are common among older Kenyans: Umenona can be meant kindly, as 'you look healthy and well fed'. Many young people in towns find it rude, so avoid it unless you know the person well.
body.so: Umependeza! (Waad qurxoon tahay!) waa ammaanta ugu badbaadsan, dharka, timo cusub ama maalin gaar ah. Faallooyinka miisaanka ayaa caadi u ah Kenyaanka waaweyn: Umenona waxaa loo oran karaa si naxariis leh, sida 'caafimaad baad u egtahay, wax fiicanna waad cuntaa'. Dhallinyaro badan oo magaalooyinka ku nool ayaa u arka edeb darro, markaa iska ilaali haddii aadan qofka si fiican u aqoon.

note.en: Plural: warefu. Mtu mrefu, watu warefu.
note.so: Wadarta: warefu. Mtu mrefu, watu warefu.

note.en: Plural: wafupi.
note.so: Wadarta: wafupi.

note.en: Plural: wanene. A plain description, but be careful commenting on someone's body.
note.so: Wadarta: wanene. Waa sifo caadi ah, laakiin ka taxaddar ka hadalka jirka qofka.

note.en: Plural: wembamba (wa- + -embamba).
note.so: Wadarta: wembamba (wa- + -embamba).

note.en: The same word as nzuri, with m- for a person. Plural: wazuri.
note.so: Waa isla erayga nzuri, oo leh m- qof ahaan. Wadarta: wazuri.

note.en: Used for women and girls; also a noun, 'a beauty'. Plural: warembo.
note.so: Waxaa loo isticmaalaa haweenka iyo gabdhaha; sidoo kale waa magac, 'qof qurxoon'. Wadarta: warembo.

note.en: The everyday Kenyan compliment for clothes, a new hairstyle or a special day.
note.so: Ammaanta maalinlaha ah ee Kenya ee dharka, timo cusub ama maalin gaar ah.

note.en: One eye is jicho; two or more are macho.
note.so: Hal il waa jicho; laba ama ka badan waa macho.

note.en: From kuonekana (to appear) + -je (how?).
note.so: Waxay ka timid kuonekana (muuqasho) + -je (sidee?).

note.en: The adjective agrees with nywele, not with the person, so -refu becomes ndefu. Short hair: nywele fupi.
note.so: Sifadu waxay la socotaa nywele, ma aha qofka, markaa -refu waxay noqotaa ndefu. Timo gaagaaban: nywele fupi.

note.en: Kufanana na = to look like. Wanafanana = they look alike.
note.so: Kufanana na = u ekaan. Wanafanana = way isu eg yihiin.

items.so: Wuu iga dheer yahay / Way iga dheer tahay

note.en: Kuliko = than. Swahili has no -er ending: just add kuliko.
note.so: Kuliko = ka. Sawaaxiligu ma laha dhammaad sida '-er' ee Ingiriiska: kaliya ku dar kuliko.

note.en: Plural: wakarimu. A big compliment in Kenya, where a guest is always offered food or tea.
note.so: Wadarta: wakarimu. Ammaan weyn ayay Kenya ku tahay, halkaas oo martida had iyo jeer cunto ama shaah loo soo bandhigo.

note.en: Same root as pole pole (slowly). Plural: wapole.
note.so: Isla xididka pole pole (tartiib). Wadarta: wapole.

note.en: Someone who makes people laugh. Plural: wacheshi.
note.so: Qof dadka qosliya. Wadarta: wacheshi.

note.en: Plural: wavivu. Laziness is uvivu.
note.so: Wadarta: wavivu. Caajisnimadu waa uvivu.

note.en: From kuchapa kazi (to work hard). Plural: wachapakazi.
note.so: Waxay ka timid kuchapa kazi (si adag u shaqayn). Wadarta: wachapakazi.

note.en: Mwalimu mkali = a strict teacher. Young people also use kali for 'awesome': Ngoma hii ni kali!
note.so: Mwalimu mkali = macallin adag. Dhallinyaraduna kali waxay u isticmaalaan 'cajiib': Ngoma hii ni kali!

note.en: Plural: waaminifu.
note.so: Wadarta: waaminifu.

note.en: -me- shows a state: Nimefurahi = I'm happy (lit. I have become happy).
note.so: -me- waxay muujisaa xaalad: Nimefurahi = Waan faraxsanahay (macnaha: waan farxay).

note.en: Nimechoka sana = I'm very tired. It can also mean 'I'm fed up'.
note.so: Nimechoka sana = Aad baan u daallanahay. Sidoo kale waxay noqon kartaa 'waan ka daalay'.

note.en: Mbona is the everyday Kenyan 'why'; the textbook form is kwa nini.
note.so: Mbona waa 'maxay' maalinlaha Kenya; qaabka buugaagtu waa kwa nini.

note.en: Lit. I have anger. Nimekasirika means the same.
note.so: Macnaha: cadho ayaan qabaa. Nimekasirika isla macnaha ayay leedahay.

note.en: Short for ninaogopa. Naogopa mbwa = I'm scared of dogs.
note.so: Waa soo gaabinta ninaogopa. Naogopa mbwa = Eeyaha ayaan ka baqaa.

note.en: From kujali (to care, to mind). Usijali, ni sawa = Don't worry, it's fine.
note.so: Waxay ka timid kujali (dan ka gelid). Usijali, ni sawa = Ha welwelin, waa hagaag.

note.en: Ako is everyday Kenyan for yuko. About looks it means fit and healthy; about life it means doing well.
note.so: Ako waa qaabka maalinlaha Kenya ee yuko. Marka laga hadlayo muuqaalka waxay ka dhigan tahay jir fiican iyo caafimaad; marka laga hadlayo nolosha, waxay ka dhigan tahay inuu si fiican u nool yahay.

note.en: Msee poa = a good, easy-going person. Plural: wasee poa.
note.so: Msee poa = qof wanaagsan oo fudud. Wadarta: wasee poa.

items.so: Si fiican buu u labbisan yahay

note.en: In Kenya smart usually means well dressed, not clever. Leo uko smart! = You look sharp today!
note.so: Kenya, smart badanaa waxay ka dhigan tahay qof si fiican u labbisan, ma aha caqli. Leo uko smart! = Maanta si qurux badan baad u labbisan tahay!

note.en: From kunona (to get fat). Older Kenyans often mean it kindly: you look healthy. Many young people find it rude, so be careful.
note.so: Waxay ka timid kunona (buurnaan). Kenyaanka waaweyn badanaa si naxariis leh ayay u yiraahdaan: caafimaad baad u egtahay. Dhallinyaro badan ayaa u arka edeb darro, markaa ka taxaddar.

note.en: Praise (quick-thinking) or a warning (cunning), depending on the tone. Plural: wajanja.
note.so: Waxay noqon kartaa ammaan (degdeg u fikira) ama digniin (khiyaano badan), iyadoo ku xiran codka. Wadarta: wajanja.

explain.en: 'You look really nice today!' – 'Thank you very much!'
explain.so: 'Maanta aad baad u qurxoon tahay!' – 'Aad baad u mahadsan tahay!'

lines.en: What does your uncle look like?
lines.so: Abtigaa sidee buu u eg yahay?

lines.sw: Ni mrefu na mwembamba. Ana ndevu.
lines.en: He's tall and thin. He has a beard.
lines.so: Waa nin dheer oo caato ah. Gadh ayuu leeyahay.

lines.en: That one over there? He looks like you!
lines.so: Kaas halkaas jooga? Adiga ayuu kuu eg yahay!

lines.sw: Ndio, ni yeye! Mjomba, karibu Nairobi!
lines.en: Yes, it's him! Uncle, welcome to Nairobi!
lines.so: Haa, waa isaga! Abti, ku soo dhawoow Nairobi!

question.en: What does Farah's uncle look like?
question.so: Abtiga Farah sidee buu u eg yahay?

options.so: Nin gaaban oo timo dhaadheer leh

options.en: Tall and thin, with a beard
options.so: Nin dheer oo caato ah, gadhna leh

extra.heard: Rafiki yako Baraka ni mtu wa aina gani?

explain.en: 'What kind of person is your friend Baraka?' – 'He's very funny and generous.'
explain.so: 'Saaxiibkaa Baraka waa qof noocee ah?' – 'Aad buu u kaftan badan yahay, waana deeqsi.'

meaning.en: Wanjiku never gets tired at work. She's a hard worker.
meaning.so: Wanjiku kama daasho shaqada. Waa qof dadaal badan.

prompt.en: Our teacher is strict but honest
prompt.so: Macallinkayagu wuu adag yahay laakiin waa daacad

extra.answer: Mwalimu wetu ni mkali lakini mwaminifu

meaning.en: I'm very tired, I want to sleep.
meaning.so: Aad baan u daallanahay, waxaan rabaa inaan seexdo.

explain.so: 'Maanta aad baan u faraxsanahay!' – 'Fiican! Maxaa jira?'

lines.sw: Achieng, kuna shida? Unaonekana una huzuni.
lines.en: Achieng, is something wrong? You look sad.
lines.so: Achieng, wax dhib ah ma jiraa? Waxaad u egtahay qof murugaysan.

lines.sw: Nina wasiwasi. Kesho nina mtihani mkubwa.
lines.en: I'm worried. Tomorrow I have a big exam.
lines.so: Waan walwalsanahay. Berri imtixaan weyn ayaan leeyahay.

lines.en: Don't worry! You've studied a lot.
lines.so: Ha welwelin! Wax badan ayaad baratay.

lines.en: Thanks. I'm just a little scared.
lines.so: Mahadsanid. Wax yar uun baan baqayaa.

options.en: She has a big exam tomorrow

explain.en: 'How do you feel today?' – 'A little tired, but I'm okay.'
explain.so: 'Maanta sidee dareemaysaa?' – 'Wax yar baan daallanahay, laakiin waan fiicanahay.'

meaning.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
meaning.so: Ha welwelin, wax walba way hagaagi doonaan.

extra.heard: Huyo jamaa ni mtu wa aina gani?

explain.en: 'What kind of person is that guy?' – 'He's a cool guy, you'll like him.'
explain.so: 'Ninkaas waa qof noocee ah?' – 'Waa nin fiican, waad jeclaan doontaa.'

meaning.en: Kamau is a cool guy, everybody likes him.
meaning.so: Kamau waa nin fiican, qof walba wuu jecel yahay.

lines.sw: Ndio! Ako fiti sana, anakimbia kila asubuhi.
lines.en: Yes! He's in great shape, he runs every morning.
lines.so: Haa! Jir ahaan aad buu u fiican yahay, subax kasta wuu ordaa.

lines.en: Is he still as street-smart as before?
lines.so: Weli ma xariif buu yahay sidii hore?

lines.sw: Sasa ni msee poa tu. Na kila siku amevaa vizuri.
lines.en: Now he's just a good guy. And he's well dressed every day.
lines.so: Hadda waa nin fiican uun. Maalin kastana si fiican buu u labbisan yahay.

question.en: Why is Otieno in good shape?
question.so: Maxaa Otieno jir ahaan ugu fiican yahay?
